name: Gerald R. Ford International Airport
before:
West Michigan's airport, about 13 miles south east of Grand Rapids, and second busiest in the state after Detroit. As of September 2025 it flew to 39 airports across the United States.

The concourses split cleanly by airline. Delta, American and United use Concourse A with its 15 gates; Southwest, Sun Country, Frontier and Allegiant use Concourse B with eight. Every gate has a climate controlled jetway, which matters in a Michigan winter.

The terminal was substantially improved in September 2017, when the first phase of the Gateway Transformation added 59,000 square feet including a single consolidated security checkpoint, a new retail and dining marketplace, and business centres and lounges.

Three runways serve the 3,127 acre site, two parallel and one crossing, plus a separate 5,000 foot general aviation strip.

The airport opened as Kent County Airport and was renamed in December 1999 after Gerald R. Ford, who represented the Grand Rapids area in Congress from 1949 to 1973.
after:
West Michigan's main airport, about 13 miles south east of Grand Rapids and the second busiest in the state after Detroit. Allegiant, American, Avelo, Delta, Frontier, Southwest, Sun Country and United fly nonstop from here to more than 35 destinations, all in the United States.

There are two concourses, A and B. The Gateway Transformation project brought security screening into a single checkpoint and added a new marketplace of shops and restaurants.

Three runways serve the 3,127 acre site: two parallel runways running east to west, one of them 5,000 feet long, and a third running north to south.

The airport opened as Kent County Airport and was renamed in December 1999 after Gerald R. Ford, who represented the Grand Rapids area in Congress from 1949 to 1973.

claims.note: Was 'The terminal was substantially improved in September 2017, when the first phase of the Gateway Transformation added 59,000 square feet including...'. The operator's own page mentions the project only in a contractor's aside, which dates it to 2018 where Wikipedia has phase one opening in September 2017, so no date is given; the floor area and the business centres and lounges rest on Wikipedia alone. For Andy (new facts, not added): the terminal has changed a good deal since, with Concourse A's eight-gate expansion in 2024, a new consolidated rental car facility in July 2026 and a $135 million ticketing and baggage project opened in August 2026 (operator release, 26 August 2026).

claims.note: Was 'Three runways ... two parallel and one crossing, plus a separate 5,000 foot general aviation strip', which makes four. The FAA record and OurAirports list three: 08L/26R at 5,001 ft, 08R/26L at 10,001 ft and 17/35 at 8,501 ft, so the 5,000 ft runway is the northern of the two parallels, as Wikipedia's own wording ('north of the main 08R/26L runway') implies. The operator's history confirms 8L-26R runs east to west and the 8,500 ft runway north to south. 'Crossing' is dropped: no source says the runways cross.
